newsitem.title: USA: Fla. governor says state case vs tobacco is strong.
newsitem.headline: Fla. governor says state case vs tobacco is strong.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles on Monday said a Jacksonville jury's ruling in favor of R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co did not weaken the state's effort to sue cigarette makers for public money spent to treat smoking-related illnesses.
"While I am disappointed by the jury decision in the Connor case, this decision in no way lets Big Tobacco off the hook," Chiles said in a statement.
"The Connor case shows why it is so difficult for individuals to take tobacco to court and win," he said.
On Monday, a jury cleared Reynolds of responsibility in the death of Jean Connor, a longtime smoker who died of lung cancer. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.

Florida is suing the tobacco industry for some $1.4 billion it says it has spent to treat tobacco-related illnesses since 1994. The civil lawsuit filed in a West Palm Beach circuit court is set to go to trial in August.
Chiles said Florida's case was markedly different than the Connor wrongful death lawsuit.

"In our case, the tobacco cartel can't hide behind the smokescreen provided by the 'personal choice' and warning-label argument as they did in the Jacksonville case. The fact is that the state of Florida did not 'choose' to smoke, never once lit a cigarette, does not entice children to start smoking. Tobacco's traditional argument doesn't wash in our case," he said.
